title: After suspension, Tennessee’s Arion Carter donating $427 per tackle to cancer charity
content:
Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter’s standout performance in his season debut cost him $3,416.

Carter served an NCAA-mandated one-game suspension in Tennessee’s season opener against Furman for accepting a flight valued at $427 from his agent during the NFL Draft process.

In response, Carter is donating $427 for every tackle he makes this season to his mother Sheteka Alexander’s non-profit, Girls in Real Life Situations, which helps fund medical bills for cancer patients. Carter’s girlfriend, Mariah Bryant, was diagnosed with breast cancer in February. He’ll also give bonuses of $500 for each sack, $1,000 for each forced fumble or interception and $5,000 for defensive touchdowns.

Carter made eight tackles in Saturday’s 45-24 road win over Georgia Tech.

“You can’t really change the circumstances you’re put in,” Carter said last week. “So I tried to turn a negative into a positive and put a smile on people’s faces.”

After discovering an injury and electing to remove his name from the draft before the deadline, he ended his relationship with the agent and repaid the cost of the flight after reporting it to Tennessee. Historically, athletes accepting benefits from agents meant permanent ineligibility, but players can now have representation for name, image and likeness and revenue-sharing deals, some of which include private flights for players’ families to and from games.

The NCAA suspended Carter for three games, but Tennessee appealed, and the suspension was reduced to two games. It was later reduced to just one game, making Saturday the debut for Carter’s senior season.

Tennessee coach Josh Heupel called the suspension “completely outdated” and “bulls—” after it was announced in July.

Carter, who also shaved his head to support his girlfriend, said seeing her go through her treatments this year impacted him.

“It really made me have a different perspective and want to be able to raise awareness and set up a foundation for cancer research and be able to do this,” Carter said.

If Carter’s play continues at this pace, he’ll have donated more than $37,000 by season’s end.
